---
title: "report(): more examples"
---
<br>

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    error = TRUE, 
    collapse = FALSE,
    comment = "##"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(saferDev)
```
<br>

### Dataset
```{r}
path_1 <- tempfile(pattern = "report_") # all the files are written into a new folder of the temporary directory.
dir.create(path_1)
string1 <- "THIS IS A LOG" # string.
vec1 <- 1:6 # vector of integers.
vec2 <- letters[1:9] # vector of characters.
mat1 <- matrix(vec1, nrow = 2, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE) # 2x3 matrix of integers.
dimnames(mat1) <- list(c("Row_1","Row_2"), c("C1", "C2", "C3")) # mat1 matrix with column and row names.
mat2 <- mat1
mode(mat2) <- "character" # as mat1 but made of characters.
t1 <- table(mat1) # 1D table.
vec3 <- as.vector(t1) # vector of integers
names(vec3) <- letters[1:6] # vector with names.
t2 <- table(vec2, vec2) # 2D table.
l1 <- list(vec1, vec2) # list.
```
<br>

### Dataset info
```{r}
string1 # string.
vec1 # vector of integers.
vec2 # vector of characters.
vec3 # vector of integers with names. No more [1] in front of values.
mat1 # 2x3 matrix of integers with column and row names.
mat2 # as mat1 but made of characters.
t1 # 1D table.
t2 # 2D table.
l1 # list.
```
<br>

### Simple examples
```{r}
# Write the value of "data" into the log.txt output file of the path_1 folder.
report(data = string1, append = TRUE, path = path_1)

# Idem.
report(data = vec1, append = TRUE, path = path_1)

# Idem.
report(data = vec2, append = TRUE, path = path_1)

# Idem.
report(data = vec3, append = TRUE, path = path_1)

# Idem.
report(data = mat1, append = TRUE, path = path_1)

# Idem. Of note, we cannot see in the log.txt file that mat2 is mode character (see noquote below).
report(data = mat2, append = TRUE, path = path_1)

# Idem.
report(data = t1, append = TRUE, path = path_1)

# Idem.
report(data = t2, append = TRUE, path = path_1)

# Idem.
report(data = l1, append = TRUE, path = path_1)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>output</code>
```{r, echo = TRUE, error = TRUE}
# Write the value of vec1 into the test.txt file of the path_1 folder.
report(data = vec1, output = "test.txt", append = TRUE, path = path_1)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>append</code>
```{r, echo = TRUE, error = TRUE}
# Error returned because the test.txt file already exists.
report(data = vec2, append = FALSE, output = "test.txt", path = path_1)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>rownames_kept</code>
```{r, echo = TRUE, error = TRUE}
# Keep the row names when writing the matrix mat1 in log.txt.
report(
  data = mat1, 
  rownames_kept = TRUE, 
  append = TRUE, 
  path = path_1
)

# Remove the row names.
report(
  data = mat1, 
  rownames_kept = FALSE, 
  append = TRUE, 
  path = path_1
)

# Keep the row names when writing the table t1 in log.txt.
report(
  data = t1, 
  rownames_kept = TRUE, 
  append = TRUE, 
  path = path_1
) 

# Remove the row names.
report(
  data = t1, 
  rownames_kept = FALSE, 
  append = TRUE, 
  path = path_1
)

# Keep the row names when writing the table t2 in log.txt.
report(
  data = t2, 
  rownames_kept = TRUE, 
  append = TRUE, 
  path = path_1
)

# Remove the row names.
report(
  data = t2, 
  rownames_kept = FALSE, 
  append = TRUE, 
  path = path_1
) 

```
<br>

### Argument <code>vector_cat</code>
```{r, echo = TRUE, error = TRUE}
# Write a vector of length > 1 using cat(), instead of as printed in the console.
# Names are lost.
report(
  data = vec3, 
  vector_cat = TRUE, 
  append = TRUE, 
  path = path_1
)

# Names are not lost.
report(
  data = vec3, 
  vector_cat = FALSE, 
  append = TRUE, 
  path = path_1
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>noquote</code>
```{r, echo = TRUE, error = TRUE}
# Quotes are kept for the characters.
report(
  data = mat2, 
  noquote = FALSE, 
  append = TRUE, 
  path = path_1
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>sep</code>
```{r, echo = TRUE, error = TRUE}
# 4 empty lines added after printed data.
report(
  data = vec1, 
  sep = 4, 
  append = TRUE, 
  path = path_1
)

# Error returned because sep must be at least 1.
report(
  data = vec1, 
  sep = 0, 
  append = TRUE, 
  path = path_1
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>safer_check</code>
```{r, echo = TRUE, error = TRUE}
# Safer checks are performed before running.
report(
    data = vec1, 
    safer_check = TRUE, 
    append = TRUE, 
    path = path_1
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>lib_path</code>
```{r}
# The "NOTGOOD" path does not exist.
report(
    data = vec1, 
    append = TRUE, 
    path = path_1, 
    lib_path = "NOTGOOD"
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>error_text</code>
```{r}
# Add a text in error messages returned by report().
report(
    data = vec1, 
    append = TRUE, 
    path = path_1, 
    lib_path = "NOTGOOD", 
    error_text = " === TEXT ADDED ==="
)
```
<br>

### All the arguments with their descriptions
```{r, echo = TRUE, error = TRUE}
# mat2 is written into the test2.txt file of the path_1 folder, with quotes and row names, followed by 4 empty lines.
report(
    data = mat2, # object to write.
    output = "test2.txt", # name of the output file.
    path = path_1, # existing folder of the output file.
    append = TRUE, # write after the content of the output file?
    rownames_kept = TRUE, # keep row names?
    vector_cat = TRUE, # write vectors of length > 1 with cat(), instead of as printed in the console?
    noquote = FALSE, # write character strings without quotes?
    sep = 4, # number of empty lines after the written data.
    safer_check = TRUE, # perform some "safer" checks (see https://github.com/safer-r)?
    lib_path = NULL, # where the required packages are if not in the default directories.
    error_text = "" # add information in error messages returned by the function.
)

```
<br>

### Content of the written files
```{r, echo = TRUE, error = TRUE}
# log.txt file (the sep argument sets the number of empty lines after each written object).
cat(readLines(con = file.path(path_1, "log.txt")), sep = "\n")

# test.txt file.
cat(readLines(con = file.path(path_1, "test.txt")), sep = "\n")

# test2.txt file.
cat(readLines(con = file.path(path_1, "test2.txt")), sep = "\n")
```
